walkthroughs.title: Agent Command Center: set up this machine
walkthroughs.description: Tools, accounts and the Command Center's Claude Code plugin that agents need. Each step ticks itself when its check passes.

steps.title: git 2.40 or later
steps.description:
Worktrees and the shared git directory need a recent git.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.git%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.git%22%5D)

steps.title: Node 20 or later
steps.description:
The Salesforce CLI and its plugins run on Node, and npm installs them. The Command Center itself doesn't need it.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.node%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.node%22%5D)

steps.title: GitHub CLI
steps.description:
Pull requests, issues and the per-repo account all go through gh.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.gh%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.gh%22%5D)

steps.title: Claude Code CLI with background sessions
steps.description:
Builders run as `claude --bg` sessions (D-009). The VSCode extension ships its own copy, so the terminal CLI can fall far behind.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.claude%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.claude%22%5D)

steps.title: Agents bill your Claude subscription
steps.description:
On your Claude subscription, agents' work counts toward the plan you already pay for; with an API key, or through Bedrock or Vertex, every token they use is billed on top, and nothing else tells you.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.claude-billing%22%5D)
[I've done this](command:acc.step.confirm?%5B%22A1.claude-billing%22%5D)

steps.title: Salesforce CLI
steps.description:
Validation, retrieves and org checks use sf.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.sf%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.sf%22%5D)

steps.title: Salesforce Code Analyzer
steps.description:
The `static` check runs `sf code-analyzer`.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A1.code-analyzer%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A1.code-analyzer%22%5D)

steps.title: Logged in to GitHub
steps.description:
Each repo uses its own GitHub account, asked for by name each time. The account gh has active is never switched, because that changes every session.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A2.gh-login%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A2.gh-login%22%5D)

steps.title: The Command Center's Claude Code plugin
steps.description:
Its hooks keep each builder inside its own worktree and away from pushes, merges and deploys, and send it back to the finish line if it stops early. It also gives agents the Command Center's skills and its reviewer. It's installed once, for every Claude Code session, and does nothing in a repo without the project's settings.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22A4.plugin%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22A4.plugin%22%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Agent Command Center: onboard a project
walkthroughs.description: Get a repo ready for parallel agents: config, GitHub account, branches per environment, source tracking and safe defaults.

steps.title: Inside the project's repo
steps.description:
Everything per-project hangs off the repo: config, branches, and the ledger in the git directory (D-008).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B0.repo%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B0.repo%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B0.repo%22%5D)

steps.title: Project config
steps.description:
The project's settings name the environments, GitHub account and checks.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B0.config%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B0.config%22%5D)

steps.title: The team template is current
steps.description:
A project started from a team template records which one. This says when the team has changed it since, and where this project now differs. It never changes the project's settings: applying a change is yours to do.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B0.template%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B0.template%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B0.template%22%5D)

steps.title: Copied-in rules are current
steps.description:
A team's shared rules are copied into the project's rules folder, each with where it came from (GH-108), and agents read only those copies. This says when a source has changed since its copy. It never copies one in again: that is yours to choose.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B0.rules%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B0.rules%22%5D)
[Import rules…](command:acc.importRules?%5B%22B0.rules%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B0.rules%22%5D)

steps.title: Every org is listed
steps.description:
Pipelines differ by client, so the config lists every sandbox Production has, with its type (D-018).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B1.orgs%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B1.orgs%22%5D)

steps.title: Commit identity
steps.description:
Commits in this repo carry its own name and email, set in the repo only.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B2.identity%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B2.identity%22%5D)

steps.title: The repo's GitHub account is logged in
steps.description:
The Command Center runs every gh call for this repo as its own account (D-007).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B2.account%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B2.account%22%5D)

steps.title: git pushes as the right account
steps.description:
gh's own credential helper ignores the username and uses the active account, so a repo can silently push as the wrong one.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B2.credentials%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B2.credentials%22%5D)

steps.title: Client data blocked at the repo root
steps.description:
A backstop. The real safeguard is keeping client data in the Working Files folder.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B3.gitignore%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B3.gitignore%22%5D)

steps.title: No client data files in git
steps.description:
Contact imports and workbooks belong in the Working Files folder, outside the repo.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B3.data-files%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B3.data-files%22%5D)

steps.title: No credentials in tracked files
steps.description:
Org auth URLs, tokens and private keys must never be committed.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B3.secrets%22%5D)

steps.title: Salesforce project skeleton
steps.description:
sfdx-project.json defines the source folders, and local tool state must stay out of git.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B4.skeleton%22%5D)

steps.title: Baseline manifest
steps.description:
Every branch is retrieved with the same component list, so a diff between branches is real drift.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B5.baseline%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B5.baseline%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B5.baseline%22%5D)

steps.title: A branch for every environment
steps.description:
Each environment has its own branch, named after it (D-015).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B6.branches%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B6.branches%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B6.branches%22%5D)

steps.title: Each branch points at the right org
steps.description:
A sandbox's name is in its URL, so the tool can prove a branch deploys where its name says (D-015).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B6.org-match%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B6.org-match%22%5D)

steps.title: Developer sandboxes are source tracked
steps.description:
A Developer sandbox is tracked only if tracking was on when it was created, or switched on inside it afterwards.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B8.tracking%22%5D)
[Open in Salesforce](command:acc.step.openSetup?%5B%22B8.tracking%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B8.tracking%22%5D)

steps.title: The CLI knows they're tracked
steps.description:
An org logged in before tracking was switched on is remembered as untracked.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B8.cli-tracking%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B8.cli-tracking%22%5D)

steps.title: Environment-specific and known-drift lists
steps.description:
Environment config is never promoted or deployed (D-016), and drift checks need to know what differs by design.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B9.lists%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B9.lists%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B9.lists%22%5D)

steps.title: GitHub's default branch is the day-to-day one
steps.description:
New pull requests then target day-to-day work, not a protected environment.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B10.default-branch%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B10.default-branch%22%5D)

steps.title: The local default org is the day-to-day one
steps.description:
A deploy without --target-org then can't reach Production.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B10.default-org%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B10.default-org%22%5D)

steps.title: Task worktrees are git-ignored
steps.description:
Task worktrees live in .claude/worktrees/ inside the repo (D-022). Ignoring it keeps them out of your main checkout's changes and out of VSCode search.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B10.ignore-worktrees%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B10.ignore-worktrees%22%5D)

steps.title: README names every environment
steps.description:
Anyone opening the repo sees which branch is which org, and how changes flow.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B10.readme%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B10.readme%22%5D)

steps.title: Claude Code trusts the repo for background agents
steps.description:
Background agents start in the main checkout, and Claude Code only starts one in a folder you've trusted. VSCode's own Claude sessions don't record this, so it takes one run of claude in a terminal.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B12.trust%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B12.trust%22%5D)

steps.title: The required checks can run
steps.description:
"Finish the task" waits for every required check to pass, and a check whose tool is missing can only report an error.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B13.gate-tools%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B13.gate-tools%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B13.gate-tools%22%5D)

steps.title: The tools the project's checks need
steps.description:
Some projects' checks need a tool on this machine that npm install doesn't bring, such as a pinned browser to draw screenshots with. The project lists each in its config, with a command that checks for it and one that sets it up.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B13.tools%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B13.tools%22%5D)

steps.title: The repo's ticket source
steps.description:
The Tasks board shows this repo's own tickets: a Jira project, an Azure DevOps board, a monday.com board or GitHub Issues, signed in on this machine for this repo, or for every project on the same site. If this repo keeps its tasks in the Command Center alone, mark this done.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B14.tickets%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B14.tickets%22%5D)
[I've done this](command:acc.step.confirm?%5B%22B14.tickets%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B14.tickets%22%5D)

steps.title: Claude can clone the repo from the cloud
steps.description:
A cloud session clones the repo from GitHub and pushes its branch back, through the GitHub access connected to your claude.ai account: the Claude GitHub App on the repo, or /web-setup in a terminal (GH-69).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B15.cloud-github-app%22%5D)
[I've done this](command:acc.step.confirm?%5B%22B15.cloud-github-app%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B15.cloud-github-app%22%5D)

steps.title: A routine for the repo
steps.description:
A script starts a cloud session only by firing a routine's API trigger (GH-69). The routine holds the repo, the model and the environment; the Command Center sends each task in the fire's text.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B15.cloud-routine%22%5D)
[I've done this](command:acc.step.confirm?%5B%22B15.cloud-routine%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B15.cloud-routine%22%5D)

steps.title: The routine's token is in the keychain
steps.description:
The Command Center fires the routine with its bearer token, kept in this Mac's keychain and never in the project's settings or git (GH-69). The token is shown once, on the routine's page.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B15.cloud-token%22%5D)
[I've done this](command:acc.step.confirm?%5B%22B15.cloud-token%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B15.cloud-token%22%5D)

steps.title: Claude Code is signed in to claude.ai
steps.description:
Sending a cloud builder a message (claude -p --cloud) needs the CLI signed in to the claude.ai account the routine belongs to (GH-69).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B15.cloud-login%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B15.cloud-login%22%5D)

steps.title: The push guard is committed
steps.description:
A cloud session runs the repo's own .claude/settings.json hooks and not the Command Center's plugin, so the guard that refuses a push to any branch but the task's, and the git pre-push hook it installs in the clone to check the push itself, are scripts the repo carries, and only what's committed reaches the cloud (GH-69).

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B15.cloud-guard%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B15.cloud-guard%22%5D)

steps.title: The day-to-day org matches its branch
steps.description:
A change made straight in an org is lost the next time its branch is deployed there. A drift check finds it first.

[Check](command:acc.step.check?%5B%22B11.drift%22%5D)
[Do it](command:acc.step.fix?%5B%22B11.drift%22%5D)
[Read the guide](command:acc.openGuide?%5B%22B11.drift%22%5D)

viewsWelcome.contents:
Everything is on one page: tasks and boards, agents, worktrees, environments and setup.
[Open Command Center](command:acc.open.home)

agentCommandCenter.openFromActivityBar.markdownDescription: Clicking the Command Center icon in the activity bar opens its page and tucks the sidebar away. Turn this off to keep a short list of sections in the sidebar instead.

agentCommandCenter.notifications.markdownDescription: Say when a task changes in a way that needs you or is news: a builder finished, a review passed or asked for changes, a pull request's checks failed or it merged. Quiet while the Command Center shows that board. Notices to Slack have their own switch, in the Settings section's Notices in Slack.

agentCommandCenter.updates.check.markdownDescription: Look for a newer release by itself, a minute after VSCode starts and then every six hours, as gh's signed-in account, and offer it in a notification: Install and reload, Release notes, or Skip this version. Off, nothing is looked for by itself; Check now in the Command Center's Settings, About, still looks.

enumDescriptions: Match VSCode: the Command Center follows VSCode's theme.
Light: the Command Center, task pages and agent pages are light, whatever VSCode's theme is.
Dark: the Command Center, task pages and agent pages are dark, whatever VSCode's theme is.
agentCommandCenter.theme.markdownDescription: The Command Center's theme, also on its Settings section. Only the Command Center's own pages change: VSCode keeps its own theme. Kept on this machine: Settings Sync leaves it out.

enumDescriptions: Normal: each part refreshes as often as it always has while the Command Center is on screen.
Relaxed: each interval while the Command Center is on screen is twice as long.
Slow: each interval while the Command Center is on screen is four times as long.
agentCommandCenter.refreshPace.markdownDescription: How often the Command Center refreshes while it's on screen, also on its Settings section. While it's hidden, and for agents' questions and autopilot, nothing changes. Kept on this machine: Settings Sync leaves it out.
